pr_title: systemctl: edit: write override files as text files, instead of stripping the newline off the final would-be line
pr_body:
I think this is the only time this is abused:
```
$ git grep WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE | grep -v test
src/basic/fileio.c:        needs_nl = !(flags & WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE) && !endswith(line, "\n");
src/basic/fileio.c:        q = verify_file(fn, line, !(flags & WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE) || (flags & WRITE_STRING_FILE_VERIFY_IGNORE_NEWLINE));
src/basic/fileio.h:        WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE              = 1 << 3,
src/udev/udev-rules.c:                                      WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE |
```
The udev-rules.c writes to An attribute, which I assume lives somewhere in sysfs.

Closes #25303
pr_comments:
This now creates an empty `override.conf` if you close the editor after `systemctl edit` without any changes.

Before:
```
# rm -f /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
# EDITOR=cat systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online </dev/null
...
Editing "/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf" canceled: temporary file is empty.
# wc -l /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
wc: /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: No such file or directory
```

With this patch:
```
# rm -f /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
# EDITOR=cat build/systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online </dev/null
...
# wc -l /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
1 /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
# hexdump -c /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
0000000  \n                                                            
0000001
```

Hm, good note, I didn't try that! Updated to only spec `WRITE_STRING_FILE_AVOID_NEWLINE` if the trimmed string is empty – using your recipe produces "canceled: temporary file is empty.", and filling the template out also fills out the final line.
Updated to manually re-introduce the trailing newline into the buffer after the strip.
Also, please add testcases for the issue and fix.
I prepped #25487 now that should simplify this a lot, and addresses all my concerns

issue_context.title: systemctl edit results in final missing final newline
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

247.3-7+deb11u1, 251.6-1

### Used distribution

Debian bullseye, sid

### Linux kernel version used

5.10.0-19-amd64, 6.0.0-2-amd64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

amd64, x32

### Component

systemctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

/e/s/s/*svc*.s.d/o.c to be a text file.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

It isn't.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

`systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online`, put in some stuff, `cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf`, behold

I guess they don't *need* to be text files for systemd to accept them, but it's damn annoying, and means you can't process them in the usual ways.

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

I can confirm from some older overrides that they *used* to be text files, so idk.
comments:
Could you give some example? I just tried on a couple of machines, but don't see any issue:

Arch Linux, systemd 251.7-4 (`EDITOR=vim`)
```

...
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf

/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: ASCII text
```

On both systems above I get:
```
nabijaczleweli@tarta:~$ cat -A /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf

ExecStart=/lib/systemd/systemd-networkd-wait-online --timeout=300nabijaczleweli@tarta:~$
```
after typing in both lines (default editor that resolves to vim.nox and nvi, respectively). Attaching typescript from sid system above: [typescript.gz](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/9964816/typescript.gz) (note also how GNU ed starts with "Newline appended" here, but of course that doesn't really matter for the temporary file, so whatever).

review_comments: we do not allow strcat() in our codebase. codeql should have refused that.

Yes you do:
```
nabijaczleweli@tarta:~/store/code/systemd$ git grep -w strcat
.github/codeql-custom.qls:      - cpp/unsafe-strcat
src/basic/unit-name.c:                strcat(s, suffix);
src/systemctl/systemctl-edit.c:                        strcat(contents_start, "\n");
```

And no it shouldn't've, [the buffer size is checked](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/cpp/cpp-unsafe-strcat/#example).

I could replace the strcat with inline strcat-but-worse. Nothing is gained, semantics are lost.
`*contents_start` is `char`, please do not use implicit cast to boolean. Maybe, better to use `isempty()`.

according to our coding style, we don't want to use C's downgrade-to-bool feature unless the type of the variable is actually boolean or boolean-like – or is a pointer. but *contents_start here is a char, i.e. neither boolean nor pointer. Hence please write:

```c
if (contents_start[0] != 0 && … 
```
so the second part of the expression is redundant. strstrip() removes trailing whitespace anyway, which means newlines are removed.
Sorry for late review, but why not to use `GREEDY_REALLOC()`??
